headline: AMD released its own AI speed tests for its new Gorgon Halo PC chips just days before Nvidia is expected to launch a rival chip, RTX Spark.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: company-supplied benchmarks that the reviewing outlet itself questions.
importance_line: People shopping for high-memory AI PCs get an early look at AMD's numbers before Nvidia's rival arrives, but the tests are AMD's own, compare against an Intel chip from a different class and include one result the reviewer calls an outlier.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that AMD released its own AI speed tests for its new Gorgon Halo PC chips, days before Nvidia is expected to launch PCs built on its rival RTX Spark chip at a Microsoft event on 7 Oct, and says it has shipped "over half a million" of what it calls agentic PCs, computers meant to run AI software locally. The site cautions that AMD compared its top chip with an Intel laptop chip from a different class, not with Nvidia's, that the biggest claimed gain, 32.2 times, looks like an outlier, and that Gorgon Halo's extra memory, in a refresh of the earlier Strix Halo, allows bigger models but not necessarily faster ones.
notes: Company claims, not independently tested; the source outlet questions them. Nvidia's launch is expected, not confirmed.
